title: 4 months building my roguelite FPS with an AI pair programmer — what it's actually good at in UE5, and where it still lies to me
author: Snoo-29395
selftext:
NULLGATE is a PS1-style FPS roguelite I'm building alone in Unreal Engine 5 — procedural arenas, bullet-hell enemies, over 800 commits in 4 months. I couldn't have hit that pace solo without AI, so instead of just dropping the trailer out of context, I want to talk about what the workflow actually looks like, because it's not what I expected going in.

The biggest win wasn't code generation, it was code *conversation*. My arena generator builds levels as floating islands, decks with intentional holes, gaps between platforms, a whole city below, etc.

The place it consistently lies to me is UE5 specifics. it'll confidently invent engine API that doesn't exist, or give me a pattern that was true two engine versions ago. It struggle to use good practices. Coming from regular web development that was weird to me, so i look how to approach the task i want to do and feed that to the AI to create a good plan first.

One deliberate line I drew: zero AI art. Every asset is from free packs (Quaternius, KayKit and friends) unified by a shader I wrote — 312px render height, vertex snapping, animation stepped every 6th frame. Twenty different packs come out looking like one 1998 CD. I wanted the aesthetic to be a *decision*, not a generation, and honestly the shader does more for cohesion than any amount of bespoke art could at my budget (which is $0).

The Steam page just went live, wishlists are life or death for an unknown solo game, so if any of this sounds interesting:  
[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5042810/NullGate/?utm\_source=reddit&utm\_medium=post&utm\_campaign=aigamedev](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5042810/NullGate/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=aigamedev)

Curious what others here have found: has anyone solved the "AI can't playtest" gap? Getting useful design feedback out of a model on something as feel-dependent as a shooter? And for the UE5 people, what do you find most hard to solve using AI rather than manual input?
